question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{5}-1.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{5}-1,$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2-\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}+1} & = \\ \frac{2-\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}+1}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{\sqrt{5}-1} & = \\ \frac{(2-\sqrt{5})(\sqrt{5}-1)}{(\sqrt{5}+1)(\sqrt{5}-1)} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{5}-2-(\sqrt{5})^{2}+\sqrt{5}}{(\sqrt{5})^{2}-(1)^{2}} & = \\ \frac{2\sqrt{5}-2-5+\sqrt{5}}{5-1} & = \\ \frac{3\sqrt{5}-7}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
